sessions.label: turn-3
replies:
The guide (the page repeats the same text four times) lists these tools:

- 5 mm hex key for the mounting bolt
- Cable cutter that cuts cleanly without fraying
- Chain tool or quick-link pliers
- Phillips screwdriver for the limit screws
- A little grease for the bolt threads

A bike stand or a soft mat to turn the bike over on will also help.

The guide also says to check that the derailleur hanger is straight, because a bent one causes most poor shifting. On a 1984 steel frame, check that before you order. Tighten the new derailleur to the torque printed on its body, usually 8–10 Nm.

You'll probably also want a new cable and housing, and a quick link if your chain needs one. The guide doesn't mention those, so that's my suggestion.

sessions.label: turn-4
replies: Good plan. Check that his chain tool fits your chain width, since older bikes and newer ones can differ. A quick-link plier would also do the job if he has one. If you use a quick link, buy one that matches your chain's speed rating.

sessions.label: turn-5
replies:
Try a chickpea and spinach stew with smoked paprika, about 25 minutes:

- Soften garlic in olive oil, then add a teaspoon of smoked paprika and a little cumin.
- Add a tin of chopped tomatoes and a tin of drained chickpeas, and simmer for 10 minutes.
- Stir in a few big handfuls of spinach until wilted, then add lemon juice and salt.
- Serve with bread or rice, and a spoonful of yoghurt on top.

It's mild, so no heat problem. I've left out onion, so there's no raw onion to bother your heartburn, and nothing in it contains cashews. It will also be good with a slice of your sourdough.

The 07:25 from Porto São Bento on a weekday gets you to Régua at 09:20. That's the best one for arriving before 11:00. The 06:20 would also make it, but the page gives no arrival time for it. At about 1 h 55 min it would be around 08:15.

- **Weekends:** the 07:25 doesn't run. Take the extra 08:05, which arrives at 10:02.
- **Too late:** the 09:15 arrives at 11:12.
- **From Campanha:** trains leave five minutes after the São Bento times, so the 07:30 would be the equivalent.
- **Bikes:** they travel free when there's space, up to two per carriage. Seats aren't reserved, so it's first come, first served.
- **Summer:** the page says to check for engineering works.
